resources.string: Audio graph. Tap to toggle magnification.
Experimental audio listening and recording. Not clinically validated; not a diagnostic tool.
AcCorps lets you listen to, visualize and record sound using a compatible microphone. The graph is an audio waveform or relative amplitude envelope, not an ECG. No measurement is calibrated.

Use a wired or USB headset and compatible external microphone. Begin with low listening volume and low gain. Digital limiting does not guarantee safe sound levels. Filters cannot restore frequencies not captured by the microphone. A/B Raw temporarily bypasses frequency filters during listening; the output limiter remains active.

Listening and recording end when the application is backgrounded, the headset is disconnected, or audio focus is lost. Heart low (20–160 Hz), Heart full (20–600 Hz), and Lungs (80–3000 Hz) are exploratory presets, not validated medical bands. Natural and Focused filters, a 50 Hz rejector and gain up to +36 dB can change the sound. The scope has an automatic, non-calibrated vertical scale; tap the graph to toggle 1× / 4× zoom. Pausing the scope does not pause audio or recording.

Original WAV audio is stored locally before application filters and gain. No account, advertising, analytics or audio upload is included. Uninstalling the app removes its recordings. Record people only with their permission. Playback uses the phone speaker or connected headphones and does not require a microphone.
Exported WAV files are not encrypted. Choose the destination with care. Exports stored outside AcCorps remain there after uninstalling the app and may be handled by the destination provider.

AcCorps 0.6.0 · Orbivia

Purpose
AcCorps is an experimental application for listening to and recording audio. It has not been clinically validated and must not be used to make a diagnosis or replace medical assessment.

Listening
Use compatible wired or USB headphones with an external microphone. Start with low headphone volume and increase gain gradually. Digital output limiting does not guarantee a safe sound level with every headset. Filters change what you hear; they do not restore frequencies that the microphone did not capture.

Operation
Listening and recording stop when the application leaves the foreground, headphones are disconnected or audio priority is lost. Heart (20–600 Hz) and Lungs (80–3000 Hz) can use gentler first-order filters (Natural) or second-order filters (Focused). These are exploratory starting points; microphone response and acoustic coupling determine results. Amplification up to +36 dB is manual, with soft peak limiting. Start at low headphone volume. Unprocessed vs Standard MIC can sound different depending on Android processing. The 50 Hz rejector is optional and can also remove useful heart sounds.

Recordings and privacy
Recordings remain in the application’s private storage. No account, advertising, analytics or audio upload is included. Uninstalling the app removes its local recordings. Record only with permission from the people concerned.

Exports
WAV exports are unencrypted. Choose their destination carefully; an external provider may apply its own privacy policy. Exported copies remain outside the app.

Contact
Orbivia · pierre.charlier@orbivia.fr

Connect headphones with a microphone, then tap Listen. Choose Heart, Lungs or Raw, then adjust the cutoffs, filter character, 50 Hz rejection and gain. Switch Envelope/Waveform for the graph. Tap Record to keep the original sound. Name the session when finished, then play or export it from Recordings.

The graph displays audio, not an ECG. Envelope shows smoothed relative RMS loudness to make heartbeats and breathing cycles easier to see; Waveform shows the actual filtered signal. The scale is automatic, not calibrated. Scroll speed changes only the visible time window. Pause scope freezes the display while listening and recording continue. Stop ends the audio session. Original WAV recordings keep the input before filters. Playback does not need a microphone: Android uses connected headphones or the phone speaker.
